Tasks and projects

A board, lists, a timeline, projects, ticket keys, epics, sprints and links — plus the checklists you tick in notes.

#Board, list, table and timeline

Every task has one card; look at your work the way that suits you.

  1. Overview shows projects and progress; Board has To do / In progress / In review / Done columns — drag cards between them.
  2. List, Table and Timeline show the same tasks; on the timeline drag a bar to move it and its ends to resize it.
  3. Dates are shared with the Calendar.

#Adding tasks quickly

Type a sentence and Doceo picks out the date, time, priority, project and document.

  1. Click + in a column (or “New task”) and type, for example: Send report fri 3pm !high #Website @Spec
  2. !high / !med / !low sets priority; #Name picks a project; @Name links a document; words like “tomorrow”, “fri” or “3pm” set the date and time.
  3. Ctrl+Shift+Space adds a task from anywhere.

#Checklists inside notes

Tick items in any note and they appear on the board, too.

  1. Insert a checklist from the / menu.
  2. Open an item from the board to add a due date, priority, comments or documents — it is saved back into the note.

#Projects, backlog and archive

Group tasks into projects; park ideas in the Backlog; finished work is archived automatically.

  1. Press + beside Projects in the left bar; double-click or use ⋯ to rename, recolour or delete (tasks are kept).
  2. The Backlog holds work you have not committed to; show it as a board column with the Backlog pill.
  3. Finished tasks move to the Archive after the number of days set in Settings → Tasks (0 = never); reopen them from there.

#Ticket keys, types and epics

Tasks in a project get a number like APP-12; mark a task as a Bug, Story or Epic and group tasks under an epic.

  1. Each project has a key (from its name). Right-click the project → Ticket key… to change it. New tasks are numbered APP-1, APP-2… and keep their number.
  2. Open a task and choose its Type; an epic’s drawer lists its tasks with progress.
  3. Set a task’s Epic from its drawer; filter by epic from “Epics” in the left bar.

#Linking tasks

Say what blocks a task, what it duplicates or what it relates to.

  1. Open a task → Linked tasks → pick the kind of link → Link a task.
  2. The other task shows the opposite wording (“Is blocked by”).
  3. A task whose blocker is not finished shows a red “Blocked” badge.

#Sprints

Plan work in time-boxes with a goal, dates, progress and a burndown.

  1. Press + beside Sprints in the left bar to add one (two weeks by default).
  2. Put tasks in it with the Sprint field in a task’s drawer.
  3. Select the sprint to see its panel: edit name, dates and goal, then Start sprint. Only one sprint per project is active.
  4. Complete sprint asks what to do with unfinished tasks: move them to the backlog, the next sprint, or leave them without a sprint.

#Repeating tasks

Finish a repeating task and the next one appears, due on its next date.

  1. Open a task → Repeat, and choose every day, weekday, week, 2 weeks, month or year — or type it when you add the task: “Water plants every 2 weeks”, “Standup every weekday”, “Gym every mon wed fri”.
  2. When you tick it done a new copy is made (checklist reset) with the next due date; it never lands in the past if you were late.
  3. Tick “after done” to count the next one from the day you finished instead of from the due date.

#Estimates, custom fields and child tasks

Story points, your own fields per project, and sub-tasks that are real tasks.

  1. Open a task → Estimate to give it points; sprints show finished / planned points and the Table view has a Points column.
  2. Right-click a project → Custom fields… to add text, number, choice, date or checkbox fields; every task in the project then shows them in its drawer, and the Table view gets a column for each.
  3. In a task’s drawer, “Child tasks” makes tasks that belong to it, each with its own status, date and assignee; the parent shows how many are done. (“Subtasks” below it are a simple checklist.)
  4. Deleting a parent keeps its children.

#Swimlanes, work-in-progress limits, bulk edit and templates

Tune the board for bigger projects.

  1. Above the board choose Swimlanes: None, Person, Priority, Epic or Project. Drag cards between columns inside a lane; click a lane’s title to fold it.
  2. Click the number on a column header to set a work-in-progress limit; the column turns red when it holds more.
  3. Select lets you tick several cards, then change status, priority, project or sprint for all of them, archive them or delete them.
  4. Open a task → Save as template to keep its shape (title, description, checklist, tags, type, estimate, repeat); Templates above the board starts a new task from one.

#Reports

See how much gets finished and where work piles up.

  1. Tasks → Reports: tasks open, overdue, finished this week and month, and the typical time from creating a task to finishing it.
  2. Velocity compares planned and finished work (points, or tasks) for your last sprints; “Created vs finished” and “Open work over time” cover the last 30 days.
  3. Workload shows open tasks per person (red when some are overdue); Age of open work shows how long things have been waiting.
  4. Reports follow the project and person you have selected in the left bar. They count board tasks (checklist items in notes have no created or finished time).

#Automations

Rules that do routine things for you while Doceo is open.

  1. Tasks → Automations (above the board). Start from a ready-made rule — finish a parent when its child tasks are done, new bugs become high priority, overdue work gets noticed, started work joins the active sprint — or build your own.
  2. A rule is: when (a task is created · moves to a status · becomes overdue · all its child tasks are done), only if (project, type, priority, tag), then actions (set status or priority, add a tag, assign, set a due date, put in the active sprint, add a child task, comment, tell me).
  3. The switch on each rule pauses it. Every change a rule makes is written in the task’s activity (“Automation …”).
  4. Rules can trigger each other but cannot loop, and importing many tasks at once does not run “created” rules.

#Saved filters

Keep a filtered view in the left bar.

  1. Choose filters (list, project, document, tag, priority, person, epic, sprint, search).
  2. Press + beside Saved filters and name it; click it later to apply it, ✕ to delete.

#Importing from Jira

Bring in a Jira CSV export; nothing is sent back to Jira.

  1. In Jira: search for issues → Export → CSV (all fields).
  2. In Doceo: Tasks → the import icon in the top bar → choose the file.
  3. Check the summary and press Import. Keys, types, epics, sub-tasks, comments, labels and sprints come across; importing the same file again skips issues you already have.

#Releases and the changelog

Group finished work into versions; the changelog and a public roadmap page write themselves.

  1. Tasks → Releases in the left bar → +. Name it (v1.1), give it a target date and a few words of release notes.
  2. Put tasks in it from the task’s Release field, or with Select → Release… on the board.
  3. Press Release when it ships: it is dated today, and unfinished tasks go to the backlog, another release, or nowhere — you choose.
  4. Changelog saves a Markdown file (Highlights · New · Improved · Fixed, from each task’s type); Public page saves one self-contained HTML file with the roadmap by quarter and the changelog. Upload it wherever you like — Doceo hosts nothing.

#The triage inbox

New tasks that still need a project, a priority or a date wait here for a once-over.

  1. Tasks → Triage in the left bar (the number is how many are waiting).
  2. Fill in the missing project, priority, person or date — a task leaves the list when it has them all — or press Accept to take it as it is, or To backlog to park it.
  3. Tasks stop appearing here two weeks after they were made.

#Workflows per project

Name a project’s stages your way, switch off stages it doesn’t use, and set rules for moving work along.

  1. Right-click a project in the left bar → Workflow….
  2. Rename the stages (To do → Ready…) and tick “Not used” for In progress or In review if you don’t need them; To do and Done always stay.
  3. Choose “Stage by stage” to stop tasks jumping ahead (going back is always allowed), and tick what a task needs before it can be Done — a due date, a person, an estimate, a description.
  4. The board for that project shows your names; a move that breaks a rule is refused with a short reason. Reset to default undoes it all.

#Portfolio, capacity and status updates

All your projects at a glance, who has too much on, and a written update for each project.

  1. Tasks → Reports shows a Portfolio card (when you have more than one project): progress, what is overdue, the next release and the active sprint — a red bar means overdue work or a late release.
  2. Press Update beside a project to post a status update: pick on track, at risk or off track and edit the drafted text. Earlier updates are listed and can be copied as Markdown.
  3. Capacity shows each person’s open points (or tasks) by due week. Type a weekly capacity beside a name and weeks over it turn red, near it amber.
  4. Burnup shows scope against finished work; Cumulative flow shows where tasks sat each day, built from each task’s status history.

#Dependencies on the timeline

See which task blocks which.

  1. Mark a task as blocking another (task → Linked tasks → blocks).
  2. On the Timeline a line runs from the blocker’s end to the blocked task’s start; it turns red when the blocked task is scheduled to start too early.
  3. Use the Dependencies button above the timeline to hide the lines.
